item.title: 1954: Kansas City Athletics Hire Lou Boudreau, 37, as Manager
item.description: The newly relocated Kansas City Athletics hire Lou Boudreau, 37, as their manager for 1955. Boudreau is a future Baseball Hall of Fame shortstop who, as player–manager, led the 1948 Cleveland Indians to the World Series championship. His hiring highlights the managerial turmoil in the American League that sees six of the eight AL teams change pilots beginning on September 14. Photo: RF (Public domain).

item.title: 2022: Moreta Traded to Pirates for Kevin Newman
item.description: On November 18, 2022, Moreta was traded to the Pittsburgh Pirates in exchange for Kevin Newman. Photo: Marshall Dunlap (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2021: Adolis Garcia Named American League Rookie of the Year
item.description: Adolis Garcia was named the American League rookie of the year while Jonathan India was named the National League rookie of the year. Photo: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2021: Rays Promote North to Major League Coaching Staff
item.description: On November 18, 2021, the Rays promoted North to their major league coaching staff.

item.title: 2020: Athletics Release Patterson
item.description: On November 18, 2020, Patterson was released by the Athletics organization.

item.title: 2019: Pirates Hire Ben Cherington as New General Manager
item.description: The Pittsburgh Pirates hire Ben Cherington as their new general manager of the team he previously was the vice president of baseball operations for the Toronto Blue Jays for the past three years. Photo: Bob P. B. on Flickr (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2019: Cherington Named Pirates General Manager
item.description: On November 18, 2019, Cherington was officially announced as the Pittsburgh Pirates general manager. Photo: Bob P. B. on Flickr (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2017: Bob Borkowski, 91, Pitcher Turned Outfielder for Cubs and Reds
item.description: Bob Borkowski, 91, pitcher turned outfielder who spent most of his six Major League with the Chicago Cubs and Cincinnati Reds, and also was a member of the 1955 World Series Champion Brooklyn Dodgers. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 2012: Chinese Taipei Beats New Zealand 9-0, Qualifies for WBC
item.description: Chinese Taipei defeats New Zealand 9–0 in New Taipei City, Taiwan to qualify for the 2013 World Baseball Classic. Photo: Tranpan23 on Flickr (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2003: Ken Brett, 55, All-Star Pitcher, Brother of Hall of Famer George Brett
item.description: Ken Brett, 55, well-traveled All-Star pitcher who played for ten teams between 1967 and 1981; at age 19 became the youngest hurler to appear in a World Series game as member of the 1967 "Impossible Dream" Red Sox; excellent hitting pitcher who batted .262 with ten home runs and 44 RBI in 347 career at bats; elder brother of Hall of Famer George Brett; member of California Angels' TV broadcast team for eight years. Photo: Orange County Archives (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2000: Mariners Sign Japanese Star Ichiro Suzuki to Three-Year Deal
item.description: The Seattle Mariners sign Japanese star outfielder Ichiro Suzuki to a three-year contract. Photo: Rdikeman at English Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1999: Iván Rodríguez Named American League Most Valuable Player
item.description: Iván Rodríguez of the Texas Rangers was named the American League Most Valuable Player. Photo: RWHmedia (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1997: Tony Saunders, First Overall Pick, Heads Devil Rays Expansion Draft
item.description: The expansion draft starts with several transactions. Two pitchers who appeared in the World Series a month earlier, Tony Saunders (Florida Marlins) and Brian Anderson (Cleveland Indians), are the first players taken. Saunders, the first player chosen overall, heads a list of new Tampa Bay Devil Rays team members that includes Quinton McCracken, Bubba Trammell, Albie López and Terrell Wade.

item.title: 1997: Diamondbacks Draft Tony Batista 27th in Expansion Draft
item.description: November 18, 1997: Tony Batista was drafted from the Athletics by the Arizona Diamondbacks as the 27th pick in the 1997 MLB expansion draft.

item.title: 1997: Expos Send Pedro Martínez to Red Sox for Carl Pavano
item.description: On November 18, 1997, the Expos sent Pedro Martínez to the Boston Red Sox for a player to be named later and Carl Pavano.

item.title: 1991: Bobby Bonilla Joins Mets, First Five-Million Dollar a Year Player
item.description: Bobby Bonilla leaves the Pittsburgh Pirates for the New York Mets and becomes the first five-million dollar a year player in Major League Baseball history.

item.title: 1987: André Dawson Wins NL MVP for Last-Place Cubs
item.description: André Dawson of the Chicago Cubs wins the NL MVP Award, the first recipient to play for a last-place team. Dawson (11 of 24 first-place votes, 269 points) bests two members of the NL-pennant-winning St. Louis Cardinals, Ozzie Smith (nine, 193) and Jack Clark (three, 186). Dawson, 33, led the Senior Circuit in homers (49), RBI (137) and total bases (353), and won his seventh Gold Glove Award. Photo: Sacoo (talk) (Uploads) (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1985: Willie McGee Named NL Most Valuable Player for Cardinals
item.description: Willie McGee, who led his league in hits (216) and batting (.353), and his St. Louis Cardinals to the pennant, is named NL Most Valuable Player. McGee takes 14 of 24 first-place votes, outdistancing runner-up Dave Parker (six votes) of the Cincinnati Reds. Photo: M. Alan Loveless (Public domain).

item.title: 1983: Hilton Smith, 76, Monarchs Pitcher With Outstanding Curveball
item.description: Hilton Smith, 76, pitcher for the Negro leagues' Kansas City Monarchs who was known for his outstanding curveball and was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame posthumously in 2001.

item.title: 1980: Yankees Trade Brad Gulden to Mariners, for Himself
item.description: Catcher Brad Gulden is traded for himself. The New York Yankees trade Gulden to the Seattle Mariners for veteran infielder Larry Milbourne and a player to be named later. In May 1981, Gulden will be traded back to the Yankees as the PTBNL, officially making Gulden the first player since Harry Chiti to be traded for himself. Photo: M. Alan Loveless (Public domain).

item.title: 1974: Padres Trade Nate Colbert to Tigers for Ed Brinkman
item.description: San Diego makes two more headline deals. In the first, it trades another original Padre, slugger and three-time former All-Star Nate Colbert, to the Detroit Tigers for veteran shortstop Ed Brinkman and two other players. The Padres then ship Brinkman to the St. Louis Cardinals for three pitchers, Rich Folkers, Alan Foster and Sonny Siebert, and reserve catcher Danny Breeden ("PTBNL").

item.title: 1970: Johnny Bench Wins 1970 NL MVP, 22 of 24 First-Place Votes
item.description: Cooperstown-bound catcher Johnny Bench of the National League champ Cincinnati Reds garners 22 of 24 first-place votes to grab the 1970 NL MVP Award.

item.title: 1966: Sandy Koufax Announces Retirement Due to Arthritis
item.description: Sandy Koufax announces his retirement from baseball due to arthritis in his left elbow. Six years later he will become the youngest player elected to the Hall of Fame. Photo: publicity still (Public domain).

item.title: 1965: Zoilo Versalles, 25, Wins AL MVP for Twins
item.description: Minnesota Twins' All-Star shortstop Zoilo Versalles, 25, wins the American League Most Valuable Player Award for 1965. Versalles, a native Cuban who led the Junior Circuit in seven offensive categories and sparked his team to the AL pennant, secures 19 of 20 first-place votes (275 points) to outdistance teammate and fellow Cuban Tony Oliva (one vote, 174 points) to become the first Latin American to be elected MVP…

item.title: 1964: Brooks Robinson Named AL MVP, First Non-Yankee Since 1959
item.description: Baltimore Orioles third baseman Brooks Robinson, who hit .317 with 28 home runs and 118 RBI, is named the American League's Most Valuable Player with 18 first-place votes and 269 points, becoming the first non-Yankee to win the award since Nellie Fox in 1959. The Yankees' Mickey Mantle (two votes, 171 points) and Elston Howard (124 points) are the runners-up.

item.title: 1963: Tigers Trade Rocky Colavito to Athletics for $50,000
item.description: The Detroit Tigers trade slugger Rocky Colavito, whose production dropped to 22 homers in 1963, pitcher Bob Anderson and $50,000 to the Kansas City Athletics for pitchers Dave Wickersham and Ed Rakow and second baseman Jerry Lumpe. Photo: Sherwood Harrington (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1959: Athletics Name Bob Elliott, 43, as New Manager
item.description: The Kansas City Athletics change managers, replacing Harry Craft with Bob Elliott, 43, remembered as "Mister Team" and 1947 National League MVP as the third baseman of the Boston Braves. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1949: Jackie Robinson Wins NL MVP, Hitting .342 With 16 Homers
item.description: Brooklyn Dodgers infielder Jackie Robinson, who hit 16 home runs with 124 RBI and led the National League with a .342 batting average, becomes the first African American to win the Most Valuable Player Award. Stan Musial, Ralph Kiner, and teammate Pee Wee Reese are the runners-up.

item.title: 1940: Cubs Hire Jimmie Wilson, 40, as Field Manager
item.description: The Chicago Cubs' major off-season announcements come in threes when Wrigley and Gallagher hire World Series hero Jimmie Wilson as field manager, succeeding Gabby Hartnett. Wilson, 40, came off the Cincinnati Reds' coaching lines to bat .353 and catch all four of the team's victories during October's Fall Classic. Wilson previously managed the woeful 1934–1938 Philadelphia Phillies to a 280–477 (.370) record.

item.title: 1886: NL Admits Pittsburgh Alleghenys From American Association
item.description: The National League officially admits the Pittsburgh Alleghenys who jump from the American Association. The Alleghenys made a reported profit of $160,000 in 1886 and finished 2nd in the AA, making the decision a fairly easy one for the NL.

item.title: 1882: Court Rules for Charlie Bennett Over Pittsburgh Alleghenys
item.description: A court rules in favor of player Charlie Bennett over the Pittsburgh Alleghenys of the American Association. Bennett had signed a $100 agreement to sign a contract to play for Pittsburgh in 1883. Instead, he ended up re-signing with the Detroit Wolverines of the National League. This case will be a factor in the player/owner battles of 1889–1890 that results in the formation of the Players' League. Photo: Allen & Ginter (Public domain).
